warnings.issue: The spec and plan still describe the pre-migration design: spec.md:67 says the PDF-to-Markdown feature was merged into pymupdf and that the runtime dependency is pymupdf >= 2.x, spec.md:111 calls Document.to_markdown() the modern entry point, and plan.md:3-4/13/21/39 assume pymupdf >= 2 plus Document.to_markdown() (and omit pytest-cov). The implementation deliberately targets pymupdf4llm.to_markdown() so it works with nixpkgs' pymupdf 1.28.2 + pymupdf4llm 0.3.4. All 17 acceptance criteria are met, so this is non-blocking; per AGENTS.md, spec changes are 'Ask First', so the artifacts must not be rewritten by Developer/Documenter without human approval.

warnings.issue: The allowed range `pymupdf4llm>=0.3,<3` admits the PyPI 2.x line, whose 2.1 release hard-pins `pymupdf==2.1` and `pymupdf_layout==2.1` (verified via the PyPI JSON API on 2026-11-18). The exact pin is reproducible, but it delays pymupdf CVE fixes: a patched pymupdf 2.2 cannot be installed alongside pymupdf4llm 2.1. The Nix dev shell is unaffected (pymupdf 1.28.2 + pymupdf4llm 0.3.4).
warnings.action: Document the trade-off, or constrain the range per environment (e.g. keep the 0.3.x line for nixpkgs and select 2.x explicitly).

suggestions.issue: README has no CLI usage/help block, and the documented usage order in ARCHITECTURE.md:105 and .gt/spec.md:119 (`pdf2md [-h] [--version] [-o OUTPUT] input`) does not match argparse's declaration order in cli.py:46-57 (input, then -o, then --version), which renders as `pdf2md [-h] [-o OUTPUT] [--version] input`. Add a usage block to README and align the documented option order.

The phrase 'conversion output and status/error messages go to stderr' is misleading: the Markdown is written to the output file; only status/warning/error messages go to stderr. The same wording appears at ARCHITECTURE.md:117. Reword to 'status and error messages'.

The 'Common errors' block omits the conversion-time OSError path (`Error: could not convert PDF: <exc>`, cli.py:107-109), which is present in ARCHITECTURE.md's error table. Add the example for parity.

The cross-environment parity claim is stronger than verified: PyPI's pymupdf4llm 2.x is a shim that hard-pins pymupdf==2.1 and pymupdf_layout==2.1, so layout/heading/table behavior (and any OCR-adjacent layout analysis) may differ from nixpkgs' 0.3.4 even though both export to_markdown(). Also note that PYMUPDF_SUGGEST_LAYOUT_ANALYZER=0 only matters for the 0.3.x path. Qualify 'the same source works in both environments' as 'the same API entry point', not identical output.

The project-layout trees in README.md:151-168 and ARCHITECTURE.md:33-48 omit `flake.lock`, even though it is checked in and is what makes the flake inputs reproducible (referenced by flake.nix:20-21). Add it to both trees.

'Currently there is no repository/issue tracker yet' is stale: the project is now a git repository (with no remote/issues yet). Update the wording. The equivalent claim in .gt/spec.md:7 is covered by the spec-staleness warning and must not be edited without approval.

derive_output_path's docstring says `.md` is appended 'when the remaining stem has no suffix', but the code always appends to Path.stem, so `a.tar.gz` becomes `a.tar.md` even though the stem still has a `.tar` suffix. ARCHITECTURE.md:70 documents the real behavior. Fix the clause and add a multi-suffix derivation test (`a.tar.gz` -> `a.tar.md`) to pin the intentional behavior.

The happy-path and empty-PDF tests assert stderr contains 'Wrote'/'no text' but never assert stdout is empty, so the documented 'stdout is reserved' contract (README.md:14, ARCHITECTURE.md:117) is unverified. Add `assert capsys.readouterr().out == ''` to the success tests.

Two error branches have no tests: conversion-time OSError (cli.py:107-109 / converter.py:74-75) and empty-result write failure (cli.py:113-120). `test_main_write_failure` covers only the non-empty write path. Add monkeypatched tests to protect the 'could not convert/write' messages.
`python -m pdf2md` is documented (README.md:67-69) but never tested; tests call `main()` directly. Add a `runpy` or subprocess smoke test to cover __main__.py.
The version test hardcodes "0.1.0", which will drift; assert against `pdf2md.__version__` instead.

TOCTOU: the file is validated with pymupdf.open() and then reopened by pymupdf4llm.to_markdown(str(path)); a path swap between the two opens could convert a different file. Accepted for a local CLI and justified by pymupdf4llm owning/closing the Document (converter.py:45-53); keep as documented residual risk rather than adding racy workarounds.

The shellHook sources `.venv/bin/activate` and runs `rm -rf .venv` relative to the current directory. Entering `nix develop` in an untrusted checkout executes that venv's activate script, and entering from another directory can target a `.venv` outside the repo. Consider scoping paths to `${toString ./.}` and documenting the trust assumption.

`pymupdf4llm>=0.3,<3` spans a 0.x minor range; 0.x semver permits breaking behavior changes (layout heuristics, defaults) between 0.3 and 0.4. Consider `>=0.3.4,<0.4` for the nixpkgs path plus an explicit 2.x alternative, or document the tested versions.

`Path.write_text` follows a pre-existing symlink at the output path, so `-o link.md` can write outside the expected directory. Low risk for a local CLI; optionally use `os.open(..., O_NOFOLLOW)` or document that symlinked outputs are followed.

The empty-result branch (113-125) and the normal branch (127-135) duplicate the same write_text + OSError -> message + return 1 sequence. A small `_write_output(path, text)` helper would remove the duplication; two real call sites make the extraction worthwhile.

Fixture helpers `_make_pdf`/`_make_empty_pdf` are duplicated between test_cli.py and test_converter.py. Move them to the already-present, effectively empty conftest.py so PDF-generation details live in one place.

resolved.issue: Broad `except Exception` relabeling `OSError` as NotAPdfError is fixed: validation (lines 67-68) and conversion (lines 74-75) re-raise `OSError` unchanged, so the CLI reports 'could not convert PDF' instead of 'not a valid PDF'.

`pymupdf.FileNotFoundError` (a RuntimeError subclass) is now converted to the builtin `FileNotFoundError` (lines 65-66), so callers can rely on the standard exception; the user-facing path is covered by test_main_missing_file.
The project description now names the pymupdf4llm converter/PyMuPDF instead of implying the pymupdf-only Document API.
`ps.pytest-cov` is now in withPackages, so the documented `nix develop -c pytest --cov=pdf2md` works (previous warning resolved).
`flake.lock` is checked in, so nixpkgs/flake-utils inputs are pinned (previous 'unpinned inputs' warning resolved).
Runtime dependencies now have bounds (`pymupdf>=1.28,<3`, `pymupdf4llm>=0.3,<3`) instead of the previous unbounded `pymupdf>=2`.
Coverage gate verified: 85.96% >= 85% (`fail_under = 85`), resolving the test reviewer's 'coverage not measured in this session' warning.
`derive_output_path` now has a docstring; remaining wording precision is tracked as a suggestion.

decisionRationale: APPROVE with criticalCount 0. The migration from Document.to_markdown() (pymupdf 2.x) to pymupdf4llm.to_markdown() is complete and verified: 27 tests pass, coverage is measured at 85.96% against the 85% gate, the CLI smoke test works, and the prior critical (editable install with no build backend) plus the OSError/FileNotFoundError, pyproject-description, pytest-cov, flake.lock, and dependency-bound issues are all resolved. Two non-blocking warnings remain: (1) .gt/spec.md/.gt/plan.md still describe the pre-migration API, which requires human approval to change and does not affect any acceptance criterion; (2) PyPI's pymupdf4llm 2.x hard-pins pymupdf==2.1, a documented supply-chain trade-off that does not affect the nixpkgs dev environment. The remaining 17 suggestions are quality/documentation refinements. Per AGENTS.md's bias toward approval, a clean review with non-blocking warnings is APPROVE; no LOOP is warranted.
